newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central sugar mills speed up crushing date.
newsitem.headline: Thai central sugar mills speed up crushing date.

text.p: Most sugar mills in central Thailand brought their crushing schedules forward by five days to December 12 and 18, a Sugar Board source said Thursday.
The move was made after some major mills in the area such as Mitr Phol and Kanchanaburi Sugar Industry asked to speed up their start dates.

"After the board approved their requests, other mills were concerned that the decision could affect the amount of sugarcane available for their factories and so they requested the same," the source said.
There are 46 registered sugar mills in Thailand. Mills in each region have different crushing schedules depending on weather conditions and readiness of the mills.
In central areas, there are 19 mills and they also have different crushing schedules.
Under the original plan, one mill began crushing this week, four mills were to start crushing on December 8, another four from December 17 and the remaining 10 were to start from December 23.
Under the revised plan, the four originally set for December 17 will begin crushing on the 12th and those due to start on the 23rd will begin December 18.
The Sugar Board's preliminary figure for sugar cane production for 1996/97 (Nov-Oct) was 60.32 tonnes and 6.28 million tonnes tel quel for sugar output. --Bangkok newsroom (662) 652-0642
